column1: Evolution isn’t supposed to run backwards – yet an increasing number of examples show that it does and that it can sometimes represent the future of a species
column2: 进化本不应倒退——然而越来越多的例子表明，它实际上确实会倒退，并且有时能预示一个物种的未来。

column1: The description of any animal as an ‘evolutionary throwback’ is controversial.
column2: 将任何动物称为‘进化倒退’这一说法存在争议。

column1: For the better part of a century, most biologists have been reluctant to use those words, mindful of a principle of evolution that says ‘evolution cannot run backwards’.
column2: 在一个多世纪的时间里，大多数生物学家都不愿使用这些词汇，因为他们牢记着‘进化不能倒退’这一原理。

column1: But as more and more examples come to light and modern genetics enters the scene, that principle is having to be rewritten.
column2: 但是，随着越来越多的例子被揭示出来，现代遗传学的介入使得这一原则不得不被重新书写。

column1: Not only are evolutionary throwbacks possible, they sometimes play an important role in the forward march of evolution.
column2: 不仅进化的返祖现象是可能的，它们有时在进化进程的推进中发挥着重要作用。

column1: The technical term for an evolutionary throwback is an ‘atavism’, from the Latin atavus, meaning forefather.
column2: ‘返祖现象’的学术术语是‘atavism’，源自拉丁语‘atavus’，意为‘祖先’。

column1: The word has ugly connotations thanks largely to Cesare Lombroso, a 19th-century Italian medic who argued that criminals were born not made and could be identified by certain physical features that were throwbacks to a primitive, sub-human state.
column2: 这个词之所以带有令人反感的意味，很大程度上是19世纪意大利医生切萨雷·龙勃罗梭造成的。他主张，罪犯生来如此，而且可以凭某些身体特征把他们辨认出来。在他看来，这些特征表明人退回到了原始的、尚未完全进化为人的状态。
column3: ugly connotations|令人反感的言外之意

column1: While Lombroso was measuring criminals, a Belgian palaeontologist called Louis Dollo was studying fossil records and coming to the opposite conclusion.
column2: 当隆布罗索在研究罪犯时，另一位比利时古生物学家路易斯·多洛则通过研究化石记录得出了相反的结论。

column1: In 1890 he proposed that evolution was irreversible: that ‘an organism is unable to return, even partially, to a previous stage already realised in the ranks of its ancestors’.
column2: 1890年，他提出进化不可逆，即“一个生物体无法回到其祖先曾经达到的演化阶段，哪怕只是部分地回到那个阶段也不行”。

column1: Early 20th-century biologists came to a similar conclusion, though they qualified it in terms of probability, stating that there is no reason why evolution cannot run backwards—it is just very unlikely.
column2: 20世纪初的生物学家得出了类似的结论，但他们从概率的角度对这一结论加了限定。他们指出，没有理由认为进化不能逆转，只是这种情况发生的可能性极小。
column4: came to a similar conclusion|得出类似结论

column1: And so the idea of irreversibility in evolution stuck and came to be known as ‘Dollo’s law’.
column2: 因此，进化过程中不可逆性的概念便固定了下来，并被称为‘多洛定律’。

column1: If Dollo’s law is right, atavisms should occur only very rarely, if at all.
column2: 如果多洛定律是正确的，那么返祖现象应该很少发生，甚至根本不会发生。

column1: Yet almost since the idea took root, exceptions have been cropping up.
column2: 然而，几乎从这一想法被接受以来，反例便不断出现。

column1: In 1919, for example, a humpback whale with a pair of leg-like appendages over a metre long, complete with a full set of limb bones, was caught off Vancouver Island in Canada.
column2: 例如，1919年在加拿大温哥华岛近海捕获了一头座头鲸。它长着一对一米多长、形似腿的附肢，里面的肢骨一应俱全。

column1: Explorer Roy Chapman Andrews argued at the time that the whale must be a throwback to a land-living ancestor.
column2: 探险家罗伊·查普曼·安德鲁斯当时认为，这种鲸鱼很可能是生活在陆地上的祖先的遗骸。

column1: ‘I can see no other explanation,’ he wrote in 1921.
column2: ‘我看不到其他解释，’他在1921年写道。

column1: Since then, so many other examples have been discovered that it no longer makes sense to say that evolution is as good as irreversible.
column2: 从那以后，又发现了许多类似的例子，因此说进化过程是不可逆的这一说法已经不再适用了。

column1: And this poses a puzzle: how can characteristics that disappeared millions of years ago suddenly reappear?
column2: 这确实是一个谜题：那些在数百万年前就已经消失的特征，是如何突然又重新出现的呢？

column1: In 1994, Rudolf Raff and colleagues at Indiana University in the USA decided to use genetics to put a number on the probability of evolution going into reverse.
column2: 1994年，美国印第安纳大学的鲁道夫·拉夫及其同事决定运用遗传学方法为进化倒退的可能性赋予一个具体数值。

column1: They reasoned that while some evolutionary changes involve the loss of genes and are therefore irreversible, others may be the result of genes being switched off.
column2: 他们推论，虽然某些进化变化涉及基因丢失因而不可逆，但另一些可能是基因被关闭的结果。

column1: If these silent genes are somehow switched back on, they argued, long-lost traits could reappear.
column2: 如果这些沉默基因被重新激活，他们认为久失的特征可能重新出现。

column1: Raff’s team went on to calculate the likelihood of it happening.
column2: 拉夫团队计算了这种情况发生的可能性。

column1: Silent genes accumulate random mutations, they reasoned, eventually rendering them useless.
column2: 他们推测，沉默的基因会不断积累随机突变，最终使其变得毫无用处。
column10: rendering|v. 使其变得毫无用处

column1: So how long can a gene survive in a species if it is no longer used?
column2: 那么，如果一个基因不再被使用，它在物种中还能存活多久呢？

column1: The team calculated that there is a good chance of silent genes surviving for up to 6 million years in at least a few individuals in a population, and that some might survive as long as 10 million years.
column2: 研究团队算出，一个种群中至少有少数个体所携带的沉默基因，很有可能保留长达600万年，有些基因甚至可能保留长达1000万年。
column4: a good chance of|很有可能

column1: In other words, throwbacks are possible, but only to the relatively recent evolutionary past.
column2: 换句话说，回溯现象是可能的，但仅限于相对较近的进化过去。

column1: As a possible example, the team pointed to the mole salamanders of Mexico and California.
column2: 作为一个可能的例子，研究团队提到了墨西哥和加利福尼亚州的蝾螈类动物。

column1: Like most amphibians these begin life in a juvenile ‘tadpole’ state, then metamorphose into the adult form—except for one species, the axolotl, which famously lives its entire life as a juvenile.
column2: 与大多数两栖动物一样，它们最初呈“蝌蚪”般的幼体形态，随后变态发育为成体。只有墨西哥钝口螈这种动物例外，它以终生保持幼体形态而闻名。
column11: juvenile ‘tadpole’ state|“蝌蚪”般的幼体形态

column1: The simplest explanation for this is that the axolotl lineage alone lost the ability to metamorphose, while others retained it.
column2: 最简单的解释是：只有阿兹洛特尔这一谱系失去了变态能力，而其他物种则保留了这种能力。

column1: From a detailed analysis of the salamanders’ family tree, however, it is clear that the other lineages evolved from an ancestor that itself had lost the ability to metamorphose.
column2: 然而，对这些蝾螈的系统树作详细分析便可清楚看到，其他谱系是从一个祖先进化而来的，而这个祖先本身已经失去了变态发育的能力。

column1: In other words, metamorphosis in mole salamanders is an atavism.
column2: 换句话说，鼹鼠蝾螈的变态过程是一种返祖现象。

column1: The salamander example fits with Raff’s 10-million-year time frame.
column2: 蝾螈的例子与拉夫所提出的1000万年时间框架是一致的。

column1: More recently, however, examples have been reported that break the time limit, suggesting that silent genes may not be the whole story.
column2: 不过，最近有一些案例表明，某些基因突破了时间限制，暗示沉默基因可能并非全部因素。

column1: In a paper published last year, biologist Gunter Wagner of Yale University reported some work on the evolutionary history of a group of South American lizards called Bachia.
column2: 在去年发表的一篇论文中，耶鲁大学的生物学家君特·瓦格纳报道了一项研究，探讨的是一群名为Bachia的南美蜥蜴的演化史。

column1: Many of these have minuscule limbs; some look more like snakes than lizards and a few have completely lost the toes on their hind limbs.
column2: 这些蜥蜴的许多都拥有极小的四肢；有些看起来更像蛇而不是蜥蜴，还有一些后肢上的脚趾已经完全消失。

column1: Other species, however, sport up to four toes on their hind legs.
column2: 不过，其他一些物种的后腿上拥有多达四个脚趾。

column1: The simplest explanation is that the toed lineages never lost their toes, but Wagner begs to differ.
column2: 最简单的解释是，有趾类谱系从未失去脚趾，但瓦格纳持不同意见。

column1: According to his analysis of the Bachia family tree, the toed species re-evolved toes from toeless ancestors and, what is more, digit loss and gain has occurred on more than one occasion over tens of millions of years.
column2: 根据他对Bachia系统树的分析，有趾的物种是从无趾的祖先重新演化出趾的。更重要的是，在数千万年间，趾的丧失与重新获得发生过不止一次。
column12: loss and gain|丧失与重新获得
column13: on more than one occasion|不止一次
column14: tens of millions of years|数千万年

column1: So what’s going on?
column2: 那么，到底发生了什么呢？

column1: One possibility is that these traits are lost and then simply reappear, in much the same way that similar structures can independently arise in unrelated species, such as the dorsal fins of sharks and killer whales.
column2: 一种可能是，这些特征消失后又重新出现，过程与并无近缘关系的物种各自演化出相似结构非常类似，例如鲨鱼和虎鲸都会长出背鳍。
column6: in much the same way|以非常相似的方式
column10: unrelated species|没有近缘关系的物种

column1: Another more intriguing possibility is that the genetic information needed to make toes somehow survived for tens or perhaps hundreds of millions of years in the lizards and was reactivated.
column2: 另一种更耐人寻味的可能是，这些蜥蜴形成趾所需的遗传信息以某种方式保留了数千万年，甚至可能有数亿年之久，后来又被重新激活。
column11: hundreds of millions of years|数亿年

column1: These atavistic traits provided an advantage and spread through the population, effectively reversing evolution.
column2: 这些返祖特征带来了优势，并在种群中广泛传播，从而有效地逆转了进化的正常进程。

column1: But if silent genes degrade within 6 to 10 million years, how can long-lost traits be reactivated over longer timescales?
column2: 但如果沉默的基因在600万到1000万年内退化，那么远古丧失的性状又如何能在更长的时间尺度上被重新激活呢？

column1: The answer may lie in the womb.
column2: 答案可能就存在于子宫里。

column1: Early embryos of many species develop ancestral features.
column2: 许多物种的早期胚胎都会发育出祖先的特征。

column1: Snake embryos, for example, sprout hind limb buds.
column2: 例如，蛇的胚胎会发育出后肢芽。

column1: Later in development these features disappear thanks to developmental programs that say ‘lose the leg’.
column2: 在后续发育过程中，这些结构会因发育程序指示‘失去腿部’而消失。

column1: If for any reason this does not happen, the ancestral feature may not disappear, leading to an atavism.
column2: 如果由于某种原因这种情况没有发生，祖先特征可能不会消失，从而导致返祖现象。
